Du:
does this work fetch('https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather?q=Erie,PA&appid=d3df5d3c92ea812769bd9ad5b87c118f') .then(response => response.json()) .then(data => { console.log("Temperature:", data.main.temp); console.log("Weather Condition:", data.weather[0].main); console.log("Humidity:", data.main.humidity); }) .catch(error => console.error('Error:', error));
ChatGPT:

Yes, your fetch code should work in the browser as long as:

  1. You're running it from a secure origin (HTTPS) – required for most modern APIs.

  2. Your API key is valid and active (d3df5d3c92ea812769bd9ad5b87c118f).

  3. The API key has permissions to access the current weather endpoint.

  4. CORS isn't blocking the request – if you run it from file:// or certain localhost setups, CORS might interfere.

Example Output (simplified)

If successful, the console might show something like:

yaml
Temperature: 295.15
Weather Condition: Clear
Humidity: 60

Bonus Tip

The temperature is in Kelvin by default. If you want Fahrenheit or Celsius, add &units=imperial or &units=metric:

js
fetch('https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather?q=Erie,PA&appid=d3df5d3c92ea812769bd9ad5b87c118f&units=imperial')

Let me know if you want help formatting the output on the webpage too.

Du:
api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather?q=Erie,PA&appid=d3df5d3c92ea812769bd9ad5b87c118f&units=imperial:1 Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found) Weather.js:9 Error: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'temp') at Weather.js:5:43
ChatGPT:

The error you're seeing (404 Not Found and Cannot read properties of undefined) is likely caused by a small syntax issue in your request URL.

✅ Fix:

js
fetch('https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather?q=Erie,PA,US&appid=d3df5d3c92ea812769bd9ad5b87c118f&units=imperial')

Key Fixes:

  1. Added ,US to the q=Erie,PA,US to make sure it resolves the city and state properly. Without the country code, OpenWeatherMap may not find the location.

  2. Confirmed &units=imperial is correct. Your earlier example had a :1 at the end (&units=imperial:1), which is invalid and may have broken the request.

Updated Full Code:

js
fetch('https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather?q=Erie,PA,US&appid=d3df5d3c92ea812769bd9ad5b87c118f&units=imperial')
  .then(response => {
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP error! status: ${response.status}`);
    return response.json();
  })
  .then(data => {
    console.log("Temperature:", data.main.temp);
    console.log("Weather Condition:", data.weather[0].main);
    console.log("Humidity:", data.main.humidity);
  })
  .catch(error => console.error('Error:', error));

Let me know if you're using this in a webpage—there might be CORS issues if you're not running from a local server.

Du:
i have a text area and i want to have text in it that goes away once you start typing
ChatGPT:

To have placeholder text in a <textarea> that disappears when you start typing, use the placeholder attribute:

✅ HTML:

html
<textarea placeholder="Type your message here..."></textarea>

This text shows up in gray and disappears automatically when the user starts typing.

If you want more control, like removing default text inside the <textarea> (not a placeholder), you'd need JavaScript, but usually placeholder is exactly what you want. Let me know if you meant something else!

Du:
is this searching for the current date fetch('https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather?q=city,state,country&appid=d3df5d3c92ea812769bd9ad5b87c118f&units=imperial')
ChatGPT:

Yes, that URL does search for the current weather, which includes the current temperature, humidity, and conditions at the time of the request.

Breakdown:

  • weather endpoint = current weather data

  • q=city,state,country = location you're requesting (e.g., q=Erie,PA,US)

  • units=imperial = gives temperature in Fahrenheit

  • appid=... = your API key

Example:

js
fetch('https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather?q=Erie,PA,US&appid=d3df5d3c92ea812769bd9ad5b87c118f&units=imperial')

This gives you the weather right now in Erie, PA, US.

If you want forecast data (future dates), you'd use:

text
https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/forecast

Let me know if you want that too.

ChatGPT:

Ah, got it — if the temperature is showing 35.4°F in July, that’s almost certainly not the actual current weather, which means the API is probably returning data for the wrong location.

Let’s double-check your query.

✅ Correct Way to Search for Erie, PA, USA:

Use:

js
fetch('https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather?q=Erie,PA,US&appid=d3df5d3c92ea812769bd9ad5b87c118f&units=imperial')

Make sure:

  • Erie is spelled correctly

  • PA is the 2-letter state code

  • US is the country code (ISO 3166 format)

  • You use commas between city, state, and country — not spaces

Checkpoint

If you use q=city,state,country with wrong formatting (like city,state country or an unrecognized state/country), OpenWeatherMap might default to a different location with the same city name — for example, Erie, CO or Erie, Europe.

Test the URL in browser:

Paste this in your browser to test:

bash
https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather?q=Erie,PA,US&appid=d3df5d3c92ea812769bd9ad5b87c118f&units=imperial

See if the JSON output has the right temperature.
